assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines. Rational pKa-tuned lipid design gave precise control over encapsulation, endosomal release and in vivo delivery, and it changed what clinicians can actually do. Impact on medicine and materials is immediate and broad.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group built the core LNP formulation and ionizable-lipid logic, MacLachlan carried it to the clinical siRNA product, and Anderson contributed combinatorial lipid discovery. Langer, Hope and Madden also have strong claims, so a three-person cap forces hard trade-offs. Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for mRNA modifications is a framing issue, not a blocker.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is extensive and independent (approved siRNA drug, billions of vaccine doses). Interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is contested; I am relying on memory of the lipid-development history and have not verified it.
Committee may regard this as pharmaceutical or medical rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns small molecules into tools that recruit E3 ligases and remove proteins, enabling drugging of targets previously considered inaccessible. It is a clear conceptual advance in molecular design with strong chemical biology and clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first demonstrations (Crews, Deshaies, Sakamoto), thalidomide-cereblon mechanism (Handa, Ito) and molecular glue and VHL ligand work (Ciulli) all matter. Crews, Deshaies and Handa give a plausible spread across the PROTAC and glue branches, but a fair split is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Many clinical-stage degraders and independent mechanistic confirmation exist, but no approved PROTAC yet, so the clinical proof is still maturing. Timing is plausible rather than late.
uncertainties: Whether Ciulli, Sakamoto or Ito should replace a named laureate is unresolved.
Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues may need different recognition.
Absence of an approved PROTAC drug may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion gives site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA-synthetase pairs. It is a general design principle for controlling protein chemistry, widely used in biophysics, bioconjugation, therapeutics and engineered biomaterials, and it matches my interest in precise molecular control.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the orthogonal pair approach in E. coli and then in eukaryotes, and Chin extended it to multi-site and quadruplet-codon systems and to animals. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed and are not included here.
assessment.maturity: Technology is mature, reproducible and used worldwide, and the original work is over twenty years old, so recognition is timely or somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Credit division among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is not settled.
I have not verified details of the early priority record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics lets researchers quantify thousands of proteins and modifications in cells and patient samples. It is a foundational bioanalytical capability that supports biomarker work, biosensing validation and systems biology.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, SILAC and deep proteome), Aebersold (targeted and quantitative approaches such as ICAT and SRM/SWATH) and Yates (shotgun and MudPIT) cover the main complementary branches. Hunt, Heck and Gygi have strong claims, so any three omit others.
assessment.maturity: Methods are mature, widely confirmed and in daily use. The field already received the 2002 prize for ionization methods, which could reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Six credited people with overlapping contributions; the fairest trio is debatable.
Possible perception that this is an application of earlier recognized MS methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly shows that sequence-specific recognition can direct the organization of inorganic nanoparticles, and spherical nucleic acids became a distinct nanomaterial class used in sensing, gene regulation and diagnostics. I know the area well from gold-nanoparticle biosensing, and the idea is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group and Alivisatos's group reported DNA-directed nanoparticle assembly independently in 1996. Mirkin then developed spherical nucleic acids and the colorimetric detection chemistry. Storhoff and Mucic were trainees and are not proposed.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well confirmed, and diagnostic and therapeutic spin-offs exist, though their clinical impact is more modest than the best medical candidates. Alivisatos may also be considered for quantum dots, which were recognized in 2023.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 prize on quantum dots affects how Alivisatos would be recognized.
Therapeutic impact of spherical nucleic acids is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing reads single DNA and RNA molecules electrically, and it is now a portable sequencing and single-molecule detection platform. It is a clear example of a molecular-recognition sensor that changed practical capabilities in genomics and diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton had the original concept of strand translocation, Kasianowicz and colleagues made the first single-molecule detection in alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered pores, and Akeson demonstrated DNA-sequencing-relevant discrimination. Which three people best represent the invention is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Commercial devices are widely used and independently validated. The field is mature, and long-read sequencing has made recognition timely.
uncertainties: Credit among five credited people is contested, and Akeson, Kasianowicz and Bayley all have strong claims.
The prize could be seen as belonging more to genomics than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures give nanometre-precision self-assembly with sequence-defined addressability. They serve as scaffolds for sensors, drug carriers and molecular machines, though most uses are still at the research stage.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami is the central discovery, Winfree and Yan contributed algorithmic and tile-based assembly, and Shih and Yin extended to 3D and DNA-PAINT-type systems. Seeman is the founding figure but is not credited in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well reproduced, but real-world applications are still limited, so impact may be premature relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Founding role of Seeman is outside the supplied credit list, which complicates fair attribution.
Translational impact is modest so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based protein profiling uses reactive probes to read functional enzyme states in complex proteomes. It enables target discovery, inhibitor selectivity profiling and covalent ligand screening, and it directly connects chemistry to what can be measured in living systems.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the clear central figure for the platform, and Bogyo made substantial contributions to protease probes. Other credited people are plausible but less central in my recollection.
assessment.maturity: Method is widely adopted and confirmed by many groups. It is recognized in chemical biology but its clinical impact is less direct than the higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: The balance between Cravatt and the rest of the credited group is not verified.
Impact may be seen as a tool development rather than a single discovery.
